transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
With the midterm elections now a little more than a week away, Democrats and Republicans are campaigning today in several states that could decide the control of the House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate.
President Trump is spending time in Michigan today where there's a key open Senate seat.
In Port Huron at a rally he spoke in support of Republican candidate Mike Rogers.
We're going to elect, I call him apple pie. He's like perfect this guy. He's like central testing. He's what your state is all about.
He really is. He's a fantastic man. He's going to be one of the great United States Senators, Mike Rogers.
Former President Barack Obama was in Michigan yesterday on behalf of Democrat Abdul Al Sayed where Obama criticized both Rogers and Trump at a rally.
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Carino Machado is back in her country. After 10 months abroad she's been thwarted from returning multiple times. NPR's Kerry Kahn reports.
On X, the Nobel Peace Prize winner was brief posting "I'm here with you all." Machado's return is a direct challenge to interim President Delce Rodriguez who took over the country after U.S. troops captured the former leader, Nicolas Maduro, in January.
The Trump administration has sidelined the very popular Machado who has said elections need to be held soon.
The U.S. insists the country must first stabilize before elections, declining repeatedly to set a date.
Edmundo Gonzalez who had run against Maduro and is widely believed to have won the presidency in 2024 says he too will return.
Posting also on X, he said our sovereign voice returns with Machado to "lead and guide this process."
Kerry Kahn, NPR News, Brasilia.
The U.S. is now grappling with the worst measles resurgence in decades with the number of cases running exceptionally high in the state of Pennsylvania where there have been numerous deaths.
We get more on the story from NPR's Shondelise Duster.
Pennsylvania officials are urging residents to get fully vaccinated against measles amid new cases across the state.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health says over 1,300 cases of measles have been confirmed in 44 counties across the state so far this year.
There were at least 21 new measles cases as of last week.
More than 250 people have been hospitalized and five people have died from measles in Pennsylvania.
Across the U.S., there have been more than 4,500 measles cases so far, which is more than double the number of cases last year.
The CDC says that the vaccination status of 96 percent of those who have contracted measles this year is "unvaccinated or unknown."
Shondelise Duster, NPR News.
And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Israel will hold a national election Tuesday with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing his former military chief of staff, Gadi Eisenkot,
who was promising more diplomacy and less military action.
This is the first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks.
A new political analysis finds it takes twice as long for Americans to save up for a starter home than it did seven years ago.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden says the down payment and the closing costs are now the big challenges.
Many renters might be able to afford a mortgage but don't have the cash to seal the deal.
And with rising rents and other costs, it's gotten a lot harder to save up for it, says Mike Calhoun,
is with the Julian Bond Institute at the Center for Responsible Lending.
For the median renter income, that requires 16 years of savings.
At that rate, the report notes, children may have moved out before a couple can move in to a first home.
The savings time needed is less for middle income and frontline workers, like police officers and teachers, 10 to 13 years.
But that's also twice as long as in 2019 before home prices and mortgage rates spiked.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
New York's Catholic Archdiocese has agreed to settle for $800 million claims brought by an estimated 1,300 people
who say they were sexually assaulted by clergy members and lay church workers.
In an email shared with NPR, the archbishop says the deal has not been signed but has been agreed to by the attorneys.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News in Washington.
